description: Partner countries that are new or surging for one product of one reporter, comparing the latest 12 months with the 12 months before. "new": the 12-month value is at least min_value (default 1,000,000 US dollars; never below 100,000) and the previous 12 months were lower and under 100,000 US dollars (no trade counts as 0). "surging": the 12-month value is at least min_value and grew +100% or more in US dollars (at least doubled), not counting the new ones. Each list is ordered by 12-month value, largest first; limit caps the rows of both lists together ("new" is filled first, then "surging"). Partners whose previous 12 months are unknown are in neither list. Use it for questions like "which countries started buying Japanese auto parts (8708)?" or "which markets are taking off?". For the whole partner ranking use get_partners (sort "growth"); for a one-call overview of a product use get_item_summary. Customs trade statistics of several reporting countries (Japan JP, United States US, United Kingdom GB) from their official customs data, monthly, by HS product code and partner country. value fields are in the reporter's currency (currency: JPY, USD, GBP or EUR) and *_usd fields in US dollars; ratios and shares are fractions precomputed from the full dataset; every answer carries reporter, currency, data_through (latest published month), the reporter's attribution, and notes. Maximum 200 rows per answer. Numbers in answers are rounded once, at the end: amounts (value, *_usd, v12 ...) to 2 decimals, quantity and kg to 3, unit prices (unit_price*) to 4 significant digits below 100 and 2 decimals from 100 up (never rounded to 0), and ratios, shares and growth rates (yoy*, mom*, share*, hhi*, chg3y) to 6; whole numbers and null are left as they are. A null quantity, kg or unit price comes with a *_unavailable_reason (mixed_units, weight_only, no_quantity_in_source, no_weight_in_source, source_gap, withheld; get_catalog lists them in null_reasons), and a missing seasonality with seasonality_unavailable_reason. The national level (JP 9-digit, US 10-digit, GB 8-digit codes) differs between reporters and between import and export; EU has no national level (HS6 only); HS6, HS4 and HS2 are shared. Import and export are separate datasets, so reporter and flow are always required for product figures. Rankings (limit) are limited to the top 20 without an API key (more is refused with out_of_scope) and to 100 with a free API key. Start with get_catalog (coverage, your access limits, which tool to use) or, when you already know the code, get_item_summary for a one-call overview of a product.

code.description: HS product code with 2, 4 or 6 digits, or the reporter's national code (JP 9 digits, US 10, GB 8; a reporter without a national level, such as EU, has HS6 as its finest level); dots are ignored (e.g. "85", "8507", "850760" or "8507.60"). National codes differ between reporters and between import and export; find codes with search_items. On a build that serves HS6 and above a national code without a series answers fine_digits_not_served: retry with its 6-digit parent.

flow.description: Required. "import" (goods entering the reporting country) or "export" (goods leaving it); there is no combined view: "both" does not exist. For a comparison across countries use compare_countries, for exports minus imports use get_balance.

level.description: Optional. The level of the code: the reporter's national level (JP hs9, US hs10, GB cn8; EU has none), hs6, hs4 or hs2; it follows from the number of digits, and a value that disagrees is rejected.

limit.description: Maximum rows in total across the two lists, filled with "new" first, then "surging" (default 20). Without an API key the maximum is 20 (more is refused with out_of_scope); with a free API key 100.

min_value.description: Smallest 12-month value in US dollars for a partner to be listed (default 1000000; for "new" it is never below 100000).

reporter.description: Required. The reporting country whose customs statistics are read: "JP" (Japan), "US" (United States) or "GB" (United Kingdom). Partners are the other countries.

name: get_new_markets
